summary: Unified financial master table. The top level is a stock financial document, which often contains current/summary fields; multi-period details are usually located in nested arrays under raw_data, rather than multiple top-level documents being tiled period by period.

structure.top_level_shape: Prioritize understanding based on one share per document; do not assume that each top-level document only corresponds to a single financial report. The top-level report_period can represent the current main record diameter, but raw_data may contain multiple period details at the same time.

nested_paths.description: Multi-period income statement array. Common element fields include end_date, revenue, n_income_attr_p, oper_profit, etc.
Multi-period balance sheet array. Common element fields include end_date, total_assets, total_liab, total_hldr_eqy_exc_min_int, etc.
Multi-period cash flow statement array. Common element fields include end_date, n_cashflow_act, n_cashflow_inv_act, n_cash_flows_fnc_act, etc.
An array of multi-period financial indicators, not a single object. Common element fields include end_date, netprofit_yoy, growth_YOYNI, roe, grossprofit_margin, netprofit_margin.

fallback_paths: Top level net_profit / net_income vs. raw_data.income_statement[] Year-on-year calculation of multi-period net profit of Zhongtong caliber
notes: You must first determine whether financial_indicators is an array, and then traverse the elements to get the growth rate field.

financial_indicators[].end_date / report_period Indicates the end date of the financial report period. Commonly used are 0331, 0630, 0930, and 1231. It corresponds to the mixed sequence of quarterly report/annual report and cannot be regarded as continuous annual report by default.

When growth_years=1 When calculating, priority is given to using the year-on-year growth rate that comes with the field (such as netprofit_yoy / growth_YOYNI); if manual calculation is required, it must also be done year-on-year with the same caliber, and 2025Q3 cannot be directly compared with the 2024 annual report.
If the growth rate field is missing, you can return to the multi-period net profit year-on-year calculation.
Don t conclude that there is only one period of data just because there is only one document at the top level.

pitfalls: raw_data.financial_indicators Usually an array, not a dict; cannot be called directly on the entire financial_indicators get('netprofit_yoy').
The top-level report_period cannot represent only one period for all arrays under raw_data.
don t put end_date=20250331/20250630/20250930 Such records are mistaken for annual report year series; these are usually on a quarterly basis.

If the database only has the most recent quarterly reports and one annual report, you cannot invent a longer annual history, let alone treat the quarterly sequence as the number of years corresponding to growth_years.
Finding that a field exists does not mean that it has been confirmed and can be directly used for the current task. It must be combined with the field type and level.
